from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Inscribed Square Problem", [
            "Can we find four points forming a square?",
            "Any simple closed curve allows this configuration.",
            "Visualize a messy loop of string.",
            "Place a square stencil on the loop.",
            "All four corners touch the string."
        ])
        
        # Define the curve
        curve = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        curve.set_points_smoothly([
            [-1, 0, 0], [0, 1.5, 0], [1, 0, 0], [0, -1.5, 0], [-1, 0, 0]
        ])
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Define points
        p1 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p2 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p3 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        p4 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        # Initial positions on curve
        p1.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.0))
        p2.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.25))
        p3.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5))
        p4.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.75))
        
        quad = Polygon(p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), p3.get_center(), p4.get_center(), color=YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(quad))
        self.play(Create(p1), Create(p2), Create(p3), Create(p4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(curve.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.2).rotate(0.2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Stencil visual
        stencil = Square(color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(stencil, "C3", "D4")
        self.play(FadeIn(stencil))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            quad.animate.become(
                Polygon(
                    curve.point_from_proportion(0.05),
                    curve.point_from_proportion(0.3),
                    curve.point_from_proportion(0.55),
                    curve.point_from_proportion(0.8),
                    color=YELLOW
                )
            )
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Mapping the Geometry to Topology", [
            "Define a square by center and side length.",
            "Map point relations to square symmetry.",
            "Rotate the square to find zero error."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#00FFFF")
        center_point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        square_group = VGroup(square, center_point)
        self.place_at_grid(square_group, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(square_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent point relations to square symmetry
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(4)])
        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            p.move_to(square.get_vertices()[i])
        
        self.play(Create(points))
        # Rotate square slightly
        self.play(Rotate(square_group, angle=PI/6))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Graph of placement error
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        error_graph = axes.plot(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(t * 2 * PI), color="#FF4500")
        
        graph_group = VGroup(axes, error_graph)
        self.place_at_grid(graph_group, 'E4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(graph_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Inscribed rectangles form a continuous surface.", 
                         "A solution is guaranteed topologically.", 
                         "Identify the diagonal where length equals width."]
        self.setup_layout("The Symmetry Argument", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual Elements
        curve = ParametricFunction(lambda t: np.array([2*np.cos(t), np.sin(t), 0]), t_range=[0, 2*PI], color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Rectangle/Square representation
        rect = Polygon([-0.5, -0.3, 0], [0.5, -0.3, 0], [0.5, 0.3, 0], [-0.5, 0.3, 0], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(rect, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(curve), FadeIn(rect))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(rect.animate.scale(0.8).set_color(ORANGE)) # Morphing
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        diag = Line(rect.get_corner(DL), rect.get_corner(UR), color=YELLOW)
        self.add(diag)
        self.play(Create(diag))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application & Conclusion", [
            "The Square Peg Problem remains fascinating.", 
            "Topology proves existence even without coordinates.", 
            "A perfect fit is mathematically guaranteed."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        square = Square(side_length=1, color="#00CED1")
        touch_points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF1493") for _ in range(4)])
        label = Text("Topological Existence Guaranteed", font_size=20, color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B1", "D6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(curve), Create(square))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF1493")
        # Simulate vertices touching the curve
        self.play(
            square.animate.move_to(self.grid["C3"]).rotate(PI/8),
            run_time=2
        )
        # Position dots at vertices
        for i, dot in enumerate(touch_points):
            dot.move_to(square.get_vertices()[i])
        self.play(FadeIn(touch_points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

outline.target_audience: Undergraduate mathematics students or math enthusiasts

sections.title: Introduction & Prerequisite Visuals
sections.content: Define the problem: Given any simple closed curve (like a distorted circle), can we always find four points on it that form a square? Introduce the concept of a 'Configuration Space'—viewing the curve as a set of points in 2D space.
sections.example: Visualize a messy loop of string on a table. The goal is to place a square stencil on top so all four corners touch the string.

sections.title: Mapping the Geometry to Topology
sections.content: Introduce the auxiliary function: Define a square by its center (x, y) and its side length s. Map the relationship between the points on the curve and the symmetry of the square. Use the concept of 'Intermediate Value Theorem' as a prerequisite to show that as we rotate the square, the 'errors' in corner placement must pass through zero.
sections.example: Think of a 'robotic hand' trying to fit its 4 fingers onto the curve. If we rotate the hand, the distance between fingers changes continuously.

sections.title: The Symmetry Argument
sections.content: Explain the role of the Mobius strip or higher-dimensional topological spaces. Show that the set of all possible inscribed rectangles (where the ratio of sides is not necessarily 1:1) forms a surface where a solution is guaranteed. Narrowing this to a square requires identifying the specific 'diagonal' where length equals width.
sections.example: A visual animation showing a rectangle morphing into a square as it slides and rotates along the boundary of the curve.

sections.title: Application & Conclusion
sections.content: Discuss the 'Square Peg Problem' status. While solved for smooth curves, it remains an active area of research for non-smooth curves. Summarize that topology proves existence even when we cannot calculate the exact coordinates.
sections.example: Imagine a digital character trying to park a square vehicle perfectly against a curved wall; the math guarantees a 'perfect fit' exists, even if the driver can't find it easily.
